jobs.occupation: Failure Analysis Engineer, Electrical (m/w/d) Berlin, Germany (Qualitätsingenieur/in)
jobs.description: What to ExpectWe are looking for a Failure Analysis Engineer, Electrical, to join the failure analysis team in Berlin (Tesla Engineering Germany). This is an individual contributor role. You report to the mechanical failure analysis lead. The team finds root cause and contributing factors, so Tesla can reduce field, production, and development issues. You work with design, manufacturing, quality, and other engineering teams, across vehicle and energy products, including current models and products still in development. We need an electrical engineer with industry experience, not a new graduate, to identify and characterize electrical failures. You use a multimeter, an oscilloscope, and other basic electrical test equipment to confirm the symptom, isolate the fault, and support root cause with Design, Manufacturing, and Quality. The right person is comfortable on the bench: probing boards, reading a schematic well enough to troubleshoot, and explaining what they found. Manufacturing experience is a strong plus. That includes production test, yield, process, or factory debug.?What You’ll Do- Debug and troubleshoot analog and digital systems with a digital multimeter, oscilloscope, power supply, and related bench equipment. - Confirm and recreate failures seen in engineering, production, and the field. - Drive root cause from the first report toward a countermeasure, with the original design engineers and the other failure analysis engineers. - Use the analytical tools the case needs, including functional test, electrical debug, and X-ray. - Design experiments to test a theory, and run them yourself or with the technician. - Document findings and investigation status. Report root cause and the relevant facts to engineering and manufacturing. - Bring prior failure experience into design reviews and DFMEAs. - Partner with manufacturing on production and yield-related electrical issues that come into the lab.?What You’ll Bring- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent experience. - 1-3 years of industry experience in electrical debug, test, manufacturing, or a related hands-on role. This is not a new-graduate role. Internships and coursework alone are not enough. - Hands-on use of a digital multimeter and an oscilloscope, and experience with power supplies and other common electrical test equipment. - Able to read a schematic and troubleshoot analog and digital circuitry at a basic to intermediate level. - Strong written and spoken English. - Self-driven, structured, and comfortable in a fast-paced lab. - Preferred: experience with common failure analysis techniques. - Preferred: manufacturing experience (production test, yield debug, process engineering, or factory electrical troubleshooting). - Preferred: soldering and rework on PCBAs. - Preferred: familiarity with common digital protocols (I2C, CAN, LIN).?Tesla is an Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer committed to diversity in the workplace. jobs.occupation: Lead Failure Analysis Engineer, Mechanical / Mechatronics (m/w/d) Berlin, Germany (Qualitätsingenieur/in)
jobs.description: What to ExpectWe are looking for a Failure Analysis Engineer to lead the failure analysis team in Berlin (Tesla Engineering Germany). This is the team lead. The electrical failure analysis engineer and the failure analysis technician report to you. The team finds root cause and contributing factors, so Tesla can reduce field, production, and development issues. You work with design, manufacturing, quality, and other engineering teams, across vehicle and energy products, including current models and products still in development. The role is hands-on. You own electromechanical failure analysis yourself, and you run the lab. You confirm and recreate failures, lead teardowns, and use optical microscopy, X-ray, and mechanical sample preparation to identify failure mechanisms. You report root cause and propose countermeasures with Design, Manufacturing, Quality, and the other failure analysis engineers. The right person has several years of industry experience, is comfortable taking assemblies apart and putting them back together, and can connect what they see under a microscope or on an X-ray to how the part was designed and built. A materials science background is preferred.?What You’ll Do- Lead the failure analysis team and laboratory. jobs.description: The German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke (DIfE) (https://www.dife.de/en) is a member of the Leibniz Association. The institute’s mission is to conduct experimental and clinical research in the field of nutrition and health, with the aim of understanding the molecular basis of nutrition-dependent diseases, and of developing new strategies for treatment and prevention.The Department of Experimental Diabetology (DIAB) (https://www.dife.de/en/research/departments-and-labs/experimental-diabetology/) and the Junior Research Group Epigenetics of Obesity and Diabetes (EOD) (https://www.dife.de/en/research/departments-and-labs/epigenetics-of-obesity-and-diabetes/) invite applications for1 Postdoc (m/f/d)starting January 1, 2027.We are looking for a highly motivated Computational Biologist/Bioinformatician to join our teams, which focus on understanding how obesity and type 2 diabetes reshape the epigenome, with the goal of identifying disease-associated genes and epigenetic alterations. Using lean and obese mouse models and translational validation in humans, we investigate how interventions such as intermittent fasting, endurance training, and bariatric surgery can modulate disease-induced molecular changes.Tasks- Perform end-to-end data analysis, including quality control, data integration and inference of regulatory networks- Analyze and interpret multiome datasets (e. g. transcriptomics, epigenomics and related modalities)- Apply advanced computational and statistical methods for integrative analysis of multi-layer biological data- Develop clear data visualizations, reports and written summaries to communicate results- Collaborate closely with laboratory scientists to translate biological questions into computational analysesSkills and requirements- Excellent master and doctoral degree in Computational Science/Bioinformatics- Strong background in biological fundamentals, including genetics and epigenetics- Experience with multiome data analysis (e. g. Lipidomics, Proteomics, ATAC-seq)- Expertise in programming languages such as R or Python- Proven experience with advanced computational methods for data integration and interpretation- Strong communication skills and ability to work in interdisciplinary teams- Fluency in spoken and written EnglishWe offer- Excellent technical equipment, a wide range of experimental methods and a dynamic and interactive research environment- Remuneration according to TV-L, level 13, plus annual special payment and company pension scheme- Family-friendly working conditions (certificate “audit berufundfamilie”)- Supporting of mobility with a jobticket for using the public transport- Easy accessibility by public transport or car (including free parking)- 30 days of vacation- Participation in the benefits program for employees („Corporate Benefits“)The position is available for 1 year.We promote the employment of people with severe disabilities and are committed to equal opportunities for them. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if they have the same qualifications.We look forward to your application!Please send your documents (cover letter explaining your motivation, CV, copies of degrees/certificates and references) with reference number 2026_W12_BA as a single pdf-file before November 8, 2026 via e-mail to jobs@dife.de.For further information please do not hesitate to contact:PD Dr. Heike VogelDeputy Head of the Department Experimental DiabetologyE-Mail: heikevogel@dife.deWe process your application documents for the purpose of carrying out the application procedure in accordance with Art. 6 para. 1 lit. b) GDPR, Art. 88 GDPR. For more information on the collection, processing and use of personal data by the German Institute of Human Nutrition as part of the application process and your rights under data protection law, please contact the Department of Human Resources and Social Services (jobs@dife.de).
